precepts.text: For thy waste and thy desolate places, and the land of thy destruction. We got destroyed. Shall even now be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants. So the land of Israel, whose capital is Jerusalem, it is not going to be enough to hold all twelve tribes. And they that swallowed thee up shall be far away. The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other, the two thirds that were destroyed, shall say again in thine ears, The place is too strait for me. It is too narrow for us. Give place to me that I may dwell. Give me enough room so that we can all live.
precepts.point: Spare not, lengthen thy cords. So when you have a tabernacle or a tent, you have cords to hold it up. And strengthen thy stakes. You use stakes to keep the tent from falling down.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
“Sing, O barren, thou that didst not bear”: that is our foremother Sarah, the wife of Abraham. She was desolate and could not have children, yet “more are the children of the desolate than the children of the married wife”, Hagar, the mother of Ishmael. Israel numbers as the sand of the sea; we outnumber all nations on this planet. Then Isaiah says, “Enlarge the place of thy tent.” Why? Isaiah 49 shows it.

“For thy waste and thy desolate places, and the land of thy destruction”: we got destroyed. “shall even now be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants.” The land of Israel, whose capital is Jerusalem, is not going to be enough to hold all twelve tribes. “and they that swallowed thee up shall be far away.”

“The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other”: after the two thirds that were destroyed. They “shall say again in thine ears, The place is too strait for me”: it is too narrow for us. “give place to me that I may dwell”: give us enough room so that we can all live.

That is why the tent has to be enlarged. Isaiah gives the analogy of a tent, a tabernacle, where we will dwell in Jerusalem: “let them stretch forth the curtains of thine habitations: spare not, lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes.” The cords hold the tent up and the stakes keep it from falling down. So many children are coming home that the land of our destruction will be too narrow, and we will “break forth on the right hand and on the left.”

And when they say we are thirteen percent of the population, that is propaganda. They may be counting only American blacks, but they are not counting the Jamaicans, Haitians, Puerto Ricans or Mexicans.

precepts.text: I will declare the decree: the Lord hath said unto me, Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee. That is Christ. Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession. See that? Heathen and Gentiles are the same meaning.
precepts.point: And make the desolate cities to be inhabited. Why do churches never read this kind of stuff? Why do apologists never read this type of stuff?

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
The land of Israel is not going to be enough to hold all twelve tribes. The children left after the two-thirds were destroyed will say, “The place is too strait for me: give place to me that I may dwell.” So Isaiah says, “Enlarge the place of thy tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of thine habitations: spare not, lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes; For thou shalt break forth on the right hand and on the left.” We are going to be so large we break out on the right hand and on the left.

“and thy seed shall inherit the Gentiles.” To inherit the Gentiles means to own them, to possess them. It starts with Christ first: “I will declare the decree: the Lord hath said unto me, Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee.” That's Christ.

“Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.” See that? Heathen and Gentiles have the same meaning. The Father gives the heathen to Christ for an inheritance, and Israel's seed inherits the Gentiles with him. Why don't churches ever read this kind of stuff? Why don't apologists ever read it?

precepts.text: And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls. So that is what it means, we shall inherit them. We shall own and possess them. And their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee. Meaning slavery. In God's wrath he smote us, meaning he allowed us to go into slavery. But in my favour have I had mercy on thee. That is Christ dying on the cross and delivering us. Therefore thy gates shall be open continually. So the gates of New Jerusalem shall be opened continually. They shall not be shut day nor night. Why? That men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles. That men may bring the wealth, the riches of the Gentiles. Why? Because it is ours. It has always been ours. And that their kings may be brought. Brought as what? Slaves. For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish. Any nation that will not serve the Lord shall perish. It starts with Christ first. Understand that he is our king. His orders are our orders. He gives us an order, we carry it out to the nations. Whoever does not obey shall perish. Yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.
precepts.point: And make the desolate cities to be inhabited. Why do churches never read this kind of stuff? Why do apologists never read this type of stuff?

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
What does it mean to inherit the Gentiles? “And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls.” That's what it means: we shall own and possess them. “and their kings shall minister unto thee.”

“for in my wrath I smote thee”: that's slavery. In his wrath God smote us, meaning he allowed us to go into slavery. “but in my favour have I had mercy on thee”: that's Christ dying on the cross and delivering us.

“Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night.” The gates of New Jerusalem shall be open continually. Why? “that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles”: the wealth, the riches of the Gentiles. Why? Because it's ours. It has always been ours. “and that their kings may be brought”: brought as what? Slaves.

“For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.” Any nation that will not serve the Lord shall perish. It starts with Christ first. He is our king; his orders are our orders. He gives us an order, and we carry it out to the nations. Whoever does not obey shall perish. That is the seed of Isaiah 54 inheriting the Gentiles and making the desolate cities to be inhabited.

precepts.text: Turn, O backsliding children, saith the Lord; for I am married unto you: and I will take you one of a city, and two of a family, and I will bring you to Zion. So that goes with the marriage supper of the Lamb, which Christians say, oh, we are going to be in the marriage feast. No, you are not. None of you Catholics, you Baptists, you Episcopalians, you Anglicans, you Muslims and Mormons, you are not going to be there.
precepts.point: But with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee, saith the Lord thy Redeemer.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
“For thy Maker is thine husband”. That Maker is Christ: “the Lord of hosts is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel”. So the Lord was never married to all nations on the earth. He was only married to Israel, and Jeremiah says so: “Turn, O backsliding children, saith the Lord; for I am married unto you: and I will take you one of a city, and two of a family, and I will bring you to Zion”.

He is married to the backsliding children of Israel, and he calls them to turn. That is why Isaiah 54:6 speaks of “a wife of youth, when thou wast refused”: refused because we were sinning. He said return, for I am married unto you, and we did not want to return, so the Most High refused us.

And that goes with the marriage supper of the Lamb, where Christians say, oh, we are going to be in the marriage feast. No, you are not. None of you Catholics, you Baptists, you Episcopalians, you Anglicans, you Muslims and Mormons, you are not going to be there. The Lord is married to Israel, and it is Israel he takes, one of a city and two of a family, and brings to Zion.

precepts.text: But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day. One day with the Lord is as a thousand years. So to us it has been thousands of years, but the Lord said, listen, it is only a small moment. It has been one day. One day in the Lord's time.
precepts.point: But with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee, saith the Lord thy Redeemer.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
“For a small moment have I forsaken thee; but with great mercies will I gather thee.” When you ponder on that, for a small moment have I forsaken thee, it seems like forever and ever to you and me. But to the Lord it is only a small moment. Only a small moment.

Peter shows why: “But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.” One day with the Lord is as a thousand years. So to us it has been thousands of years of being forsaken, but the Lord says, listen, it is only a small moment. It has been one day in the Lord’s time.

And the small moment ends in a gathering: “with great mercies will I gather thee.” He is going to gather us. That is what Christ dying on the cross is about, gathering us back together again.

precepts.text: And I will set my face against you, and ye shall be slain before your enemies: they that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you. That is a little wrath. And in a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment.
precepts.point: But with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee, saith the Lord thy Redeemer.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
“In a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment”. That is called slavery. When he hid his face, that is the chains. That is the ships. That is poverty, sickness, death, destruction. That is what all of that sums up right there. Leviticus shows what the little wrath looks like: “And I will set my face against you, and ye shall be slain before your enemies: they that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you.”

That is a little wrath: slain before our enemies, ruled by them that hate us. And while he hid his face, Psalm 50 shows he kept silence over the wicked who took his covenant in their mouth: “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself”. God is not intervening in some things. He stays silent, because this is the time for us to get our lives together and repent, to put the pieces of the puzzle in the Bible together. So the so-called white man thought God was like him. “but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes”, and that is what is happening now.

But the little wrath is only for a moment. Isaiah 54:8 ends: “but with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee, saith the Lord thy Redeemer.”

precepts.text: And the foundations of the wall of the city were garnished with all manner of precious stones. The first foundation was jasper; the second, sapphire; the third, a chalcedony; the fourth, an emerald; The fifth, sardonyx; the sixth, sardius; the seventh, chrysolite; the eighth, beryl; the ninth, a topaz; the tenth, a chrysoprasus; the eleventh, a jacinth; the twelfth, an amethyst.
precepts.point: And all thy children shall be taught of the Lord; and great shall be the peace of thy children.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
Isaiah says to the afflicted, “I will lay thy stones with fair colours, and lay thy foundations with sapphires.” That is the kingdom. The Lord will lay our foundations with stones and rubies and emeralds; we are going to have a crown.

John saw that same kingdom: “And the foundations of the wall of the city were garnished with all manner of precious stones.” He names them one by one: “The first foundation was jasper; the second, sapphire; the third, a chalcedony; the fourth, an emerald; The fifth, sardonyx; the sixth, sardius; the seventh, chrysolite; the eighth, beryl; the ninth, a topaz; the tenth, a chrysoprasus; the eleventh, a jacinth; the twelfth, an amethyst.” The sapphire Isaiah promised is right there in the second foundation.

Then Isaiah goes on: “I will make thy windows of agates, and thy gates of carbuncles, and all thy borders of pleasant stones.” These are more precious stones, rubies and diamonds. The twelve tribes of Israel are the afflicted, “tossed with tempest, and not comforted”, and we have not been comforted. But the mountains shall depart, meaning destruction, while the Lord’s kindness does not depart from Israel. The city garnished with precious stones is what he is building for the people he has mercy on.

precepts.text: And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people, and there will I plead with you face to face. So when he pleads with us face to face, that means all thy children shall be taught of the Lord.
precepts.point: And all thy children shall be taught of the Lord; and great shall be the peace of thy children.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
Isaiah says, “And all thy children shall be taught of the Lord; and great shall be the peace of thy children.” Ezekiel shows how that teaching will happen: “And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people, and there will I plead with you face to face.”

When the Lord pleads with us face to face, that is when all the children of Israel shall be taught of the Lord. He brings the twelve tribes out and teaches them himself.

And the peace that follows is the rest of Isaiah’s promise: “In righteousness shalt thou be established: thou shalt be far from oppression; for thou shalt not fear: and from terror; for it shall not come near thee.” The twelve tribes shall be established, far from oppression, and terror shall no more come near us. Today our people are still terrorized, hanged from trees and called suicides, but the day of being taught face to face by the Lord is the day that ends.

precepts.text: For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known. So the glass is talking about the Bible. We do not understand everything in here. And even when I say that, there are different levels. There are double meanings to many scriptures. But when the Lord returns, then shall we know. What does that last part mean? He created us from the beginning. Before the earth was made, he created us.
precepts.point: And all thy children shall be taught of the Lord; and great shall be the peace of thy children.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
“For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face.” The glass is talking about the Bible. We do not understand everything in it. Even in saying that, there are different levels, and there are double meanings to many scriptures.

“now I know in part”: we know partially. “but then shall I know”: when the Lord returns, then shall we know. That is the face to face of Ezekiel 20:35, when he pleads with us face to face, and it is how “all thy children shall be taught of the Lord.”

“even as also I am known.” What does that part mean? He created us from the beginning. Before the earth was made, he created us. He already knows us fully; when he returns we will know as we are known, and the children of Israel will be taught of the Lord himself.

precepts.text: For a small moment have I forsaken thee, but with great mercies will I gather thee; in a little wrath I hid my face for a moment.
precepts.point: One day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day. By that measure eighty years is under two hours to God. That is why God calls our trials a small moment.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
“For a small moment have I forsaken thee; but with great mercies will I gather thee.” A small moment. That is why God says small moment: it is not even two hours to him, not even a day to him. If a thousand years is as one day with the Lord, our whole captivity is a moment in his eyes.

“In a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment; but with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee, saith the Lord thy Redeemer.” For a moment. Start thinking like that: I'm only here for a short while.

And since it is only a moment, Peter gives the wisdom Christ put in his mouth: “Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time”. The real exaltation we want is when we go back to him: a crown from God Almighty, and you can't get any higher than that. “Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.” He knows you only have a short amount of time here.

Right after that comes “your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”, because Satan is looking for the prideful, the ones who think they know more than God in the little time they have been here. We stress over three to five business days and get mad when Amazon doesn't deliver in two. God's small moment calls for humility, not pride.

precepts.text: I have created the smith that bringeth forth an instrument, and I have created the waster to destroy.
precepts.point: Esau's blessing is by thy sword shalt thou live; he takes the fatness of the earth by violence.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
“Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work”. The Lord is over all of it. He puts it on Satan, his emissary, and Satan passes it around. It is twofold: it speaks of the brass and iron of Tubal-cain, and then it names something more.

Notice “an instrument”: not all weaponry, one in particular. Then he names it: “and I have created the waster to destroy”. What weapon at that time could have been called the waster? Nothing. Zechariah describes it: “Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall consume away in their holes, and their tongue shall consume away in their mouth.” Nobody could have imagined such a weapon then. They had no word for nuclear weapons or atoms, so they saw visions and explained them the best they could: it is the waster.

Malachi says, “behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble”: Esau, the other nations, and rebellious Israel that does not repent. The day that cometh burns them so “it shall leave them neither root nor branch”. A fire leaves ash; this leaves nothing. Peter says “the elements shall melt with fervent heat”. The nations know it: their treaties against nuclear proliferation show the Lord staying their hand, because whoever uses one ends the world as they know it. Isaiah 29 says the strangers “shall be like small dust” and it shall be “at an instant suddenly”, not like regular fire, and all the nations that fight against Ariel, the lion of God, “even all that fight against her and her munition”, her weapons, “shall be as a dream of a night vision”, gone that quick. They filled their bellies and lived deliciously, and in an instant it is all gone. God put it in their spirit to make that thing, and he will use their own weapon, the thing that gave them their power and respect, to end them.

This should move us. The Lord “is longsuffering to us-ward”; the day waits until the set number is sealed, and it comes “as a thief in the night.” “Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness”? Paul says the same: “let us watch and be sober”: do not drink of her wine, do not sleep thinking you are an American and nothing can touch you. “For God hath not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ”. So “comfort yourselves together, and edify one another”: this is the time to be more united, not divided over simple issues. We look boldly for that day, because “we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness”: a baptism by fire that cleanses the evil and makes the earth fit for the kingdom.

precepts.text: I have created the smith, and I have created the waster to destroy.
precepts.point: Tubal-cain worked brass and iron, and Lamech boasted of slaying a man. Weaponry came through Cain's line to Esau, who lives by the sword and breaks his brother's yoke.

note.label: War of the Gods

precepts.why:
“Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work”. Who created Cain, Lamech and Esau? Christ did. He gave them the ability to have dominion and power, principalities, spiritual wickedness in high places.

That is why the class went first to Genesis 4, where Tubal-cain was “an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”. Isaiah, prophesying of the days to come, speaks of that same smith: the maker of weapons that began with Tubal-cain and Lamech.

Then the verse goes further: “and I have created the waster to destroy.” There is the smith, and there is the waster. An arrow, a dart, a knife or a sword does not destroy by itself; the waster destroys. God made the one who forges the weapon and the one who uses it to lay waste.

So when Edom builds Space Command in Huntsville and calls it Rocket City, when his weaponry is twenty years ahead of anything we know, remember Christ said he created the smith and the waster. “Babylon, the glory of kingdoms” draws every nation that wants a piece of the American dream, and the dragon gives power to the beast: the devil himself gives power to the beast, the white man. “And it was given unto him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them: and power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations.” Even that power was given him.

Our war is not according to flesh and blood. His weapons are not only for fighting other nations; they are to force white supremacy into our minds and spirits, until most of our people in the four corners of the earth worship the white man, even in congregations where everyone looks like them. But the Lord reminds us that they are men and not God, and their pride is the thing that brings them down.

precepts.text: God created the smith who brings forth the weapon and the waster to destroy.
precepts.point: Once Esau falls, he will never rise again.

note.label: Political Power Under Darkness

precepts.why:
“Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers; that they do not rise, nor possess the land, nor fill the face of the world with cities.” “For I will rise up against them, saith the Lord of hosts, and cut off from Babylon the name, and remnant, and son, and nephew.” To cut them off means he is going to kill all of them. When Esau falls, Esau will never rise back again.

Some think Esau will never fall. You forgot what happened to the Babylonians, the Persians and Medes, the Greeks, Rome and Egypt, all superpowers in their time. America has bombs, lasers, all types of weapons, the most powerful military on the planet. But the Most High is more powerful than America.

Isaiah shows how he does it: “Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy.” The smith today is what you call the scientist who makes weapons. Back then they were called smiths; they bring forth the instrument for the work. And the waster is nuclear power. God let them create the waster, and it is made to destroy.

Job shows it striking the wicked: “He shall flee from the iron weapon, and the bow of steel shall strike him through.” The iron weapon is the missile.

So the slaughter prepared for Esau’s children is by the very weapons God allowed their own smiths to make. Nobody is innocent, and whatever evil was done to the Israelites, no one is getting away with it.

precepts.text: No weapon formed against thee shall prosper, and every tongue against thee shall be condemned.
precepts.point: Israel must overcome its addictions and wait for that power, not act before its time.

note.label: Political Power Under Darkness

precepts.why:
“And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations.” Some do not understand what that power is going to give us, so Isaiah shows it. Read verse 16 first: “Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy.” That is talking about the nuclear weapon.

Then: “No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper.” Think about it: Esau shoots a nuclear weapon and you walk right through it. That is what you call power. When he says power, some of you have no idea what that means. That is power.

Can their weapons prosper against us today? Yes. That is why we must wait for that power. And it goes on: “and every tongue that shall rise against thee in judgment thou shalt condemn.” In that day, let me hear somebody rise against us with his tongue. I double dare you. Every tongue will be condemned.

“This is the heritage of the servants of the Lord, and their righteousness is of me, saith the Lord.” This is our heritage. We are the servants, and our righteousness is of the Most High.

So overcome whatever you are fighting: drug addiction, alcohol addiction, woman addiction, men addiction. Keep his works, his laws, unto the end, which is either you die in this or Christ comes back. Now is not the time to pick up knives and guns; a gun or a little knife cannot do anything but get you killed. We wait in faith for that spiritual power, and then we rule the nations with a rod of iron and break them to shivers like the vessels of a potter.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 9 Explained Pt. 2

precepts.why:
Everything we are looking at is all in the Most High's hands. The Lord is angry now, and he is getting ready to bring serious devastation to deliver his people out of Egypt, out of the bondage, with a mighty hand. “Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire,” The smith is the blacksmith, a man that made weapons; the Lord said, I created that thing. Blowing the coals in the fire is to make the steel hot so you can bend it and shape it and make swords, shields, bucklers, battle axes, weapons of war. “and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work;” He is going to cause this smith to bring forth an instrument for his work, and his work is to deliver the Israelites. “and I have created the waster to destroy.” The waster is the instrument he caused these smiths to make: that is what you were just looking at on the screen, the nuclear bomb. God caused the smith to create that, and they are not going to be able to stop it. The Most High is going to cause them to use those weapons on each other while he delivers us. That is what Revelation is talking about: he is going to deliver us up while the bombs are coming; ten thousand on one side, you are going to see people dying, like Psalms 91: only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked. He created the waster to destroy the enemies.

“No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper;” No weapon that is formed against the children of Israel shall prosper. The Most High said it shall not come nigh thee; that goes back to Psalms 91: destruction shall come, a thousand shall fall at thy side and ten thousand at thy right hand, but it shall not come nigh thee. “and every tongue that shall rise against thee in judgment thou shalt condemn.” The Most High means business. So we have nothing to worry about, brothers and sisters. The Lord is our power, the Lord is our shepherd, and we ain't going to lack nothing. Keep your minds up.

Spare not, lengthen thy cords. So when you have a tabernacle or a tent, you have cords to hold it up. And strengthen thy stakes. You use stakes to keep the tent from falling down.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: For thou shalt break forth on the right hand and on the left. We are going to be so large we are going to break out on the right hand and the left.
And thy seed shall inherit the Gentiles. Inherit the Gentiles means to own them, possess them.
And make the desolate cities to be inhabited. Why do churches never read this kind of stuff? Why do apologists never read this type of stuff?

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: Fear not; for thou shalt not be ashamed. You see it says fear not. Why is he saying that? Because he is letting us know that in the future there will be things that, to the natural man, will put us in fear. He is letting us know: fear not.
Why is he saying thou shalt not be ashamed? Because there will be things occurring that might seem to cause us to be ashamed.
Neither be thou confounded. Why does it say neither be thou confounded? Because there will be things in the future that might confound us. But he is telling us they will not confound you.
For thou shalt not be put to shame: for thou shalt forget the shame of thy youth. We are going to forget the sins of our youth. And shalt not remember the reproach of thy widowhood any more.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: For thy Maker is thine husband. That Maker there is talking about Christ. The Lord of hosts is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel; The God of the whole earth shall he be called. So the Lord was never married to all nations on the earth. He was only married to Israel.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: For the Lord hath called thee as a woman forsaken and grieved in spirit. So the twelve tribes of Israel are represented as a woman forsaken and grieved in spirit. Grieved with what? Lies, poverty, death and destruction.

And a wife of youth, when thou wast refused, saith thy God. Refused because we were sinning. The Lord refused us. That is why we just read, Return, O backsliding children, for I am married unto you. We did not want to return. So the Most High refused us.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: For a small moment have I forsaken thee. And when you ponder on that, for a small moment have I forsaken thee. It seems like forever and ever to you and me, but to the Lord it is only a small moment. Only a small moment.
But with great mercies will I gather thee. He is going to gather us. That is what Christ dying on the cross is about, gathering us back together again.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: In a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment. That is called slavery. When he hid his face, that is the chains. That is the ships. That is poverty, sickness, death, destruction. That is what all of that sums up right there.
But with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee, saith the Lord thy Redeemer.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: For this is as the waters of Noah unto me. This is the Lord speaking through Isaiah.
For as I have sworn that the waters of Noah should no more go over the earth. So he promised the waters of Noah would no more go over the earth.
So have I sworn that I would not be wroth with thee, nor rebuke thee. That he would not punish us.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: For the mountains shall depart. Meaning destruction. Destroyed. And the hills be removed.
But my kindness shall not depart from thee. But God's kindness shall not depart from the twelve tribes of Israel.
Neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, saith the Lord that hath mercy on thee. So the Lord is having mercy on the twelve tribes of Israel.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: O thou afflicted. Although we are afflicted, O thou afflicted, that is us. We are the afflicted. Tossed with tempest, and not comforted. We have not been comforted.
Behold, I will lay thy stones with fair colours. See that? We are going to have a crown. Rubies and emeralds. And lay thy foundations with sapphires. That is the kingdom.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: And I will make thy windows of agates, and thy gates of carbuncles. These are more precious stones. And all thy borders of pleasant stones. Meaning rubies and diamonds.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: And all thy children shall be taught of the Lord; and great shall be the peace of thy children.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: In righteousness shalt thou be established. The twelve tribes shall be established.
Thou shalt be far from oppression. We shall be far from oppression.
For thou shalt not fear. And we shall not fear. And from terror; for it shall not come near thee. Terror shall no more come near us.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: Behold, they shall surely gather together, but not by me. So the nations shall gather together, but not by the Lord.
Whosoever shall gather together against thee shall fall for thy sake.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: Behold, they shall surely gather together. The nations shall gather together. But not by me. Whosoever shall gather together against thee shall fall for thy sake. Now, what is the Lord going to do? Watch this.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire. Oppenheimer is the one that created the atom bomb, the first one. And since then it has grown. Their technology has been enhanced, on another level of nuclear beyond the atom bomb. So a smith is somebody that makes weapons. Oppenheimer created the greatest weapon that ever existed, a bomb.
And that bringeth forth an instrument for his work. That is the bomb. That is the nuclear weapons.

And I have created the waster to destroy. Stop right there. I have created the waster to destroy. What does he mean, the waster? Mean massive destruction? You mean like the flood? No, I do not mean like the flood. Worse than the flood.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper. Now what is he talking about? The nuclear weapons. That is the context. You know what is funny about that? In church they go, no weapon formed. So you gossiping, that is not going to affect me. It is not talking about gossip. He is not talking about that. When you read it in context, he is talking about nuclear fire.
And every tongue that shall rise against thee in judgment thou shalt condemn. Because we are going to have power. When these nations raise their lips against us, we are going to condemn them.
This is the heritage of the servants of the Lord. This is our heritage, brothers and sisters.
And their righteousness is of me, saith the Lord. Our righteousness is of the Lord.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

points: What does the flood of Noah represent? In a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment: the thee is Israel. I have wrath upon you, put you in captivity; even now we're in captivity. But with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

points: For this is as the waters of Noah unto me: for as I have sworn that the waters of Noah should no more go over the earth, so have I sworn that I would not be wroth with thee, nor rebuke thee. The Lord flooded the earth and made a vow with the rainbow that he would never flood the earth again. Likewise, he will never put us in captivity again once we get delivered. You will not see slavery ever again. You're going to be ruling forever. This is the last go around. No more of this captivity stuff.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

points: For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed: that means destruction, no more nations. But my kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed. The rainbow itself was a sign that God would not flood the earth again, but also tied into the mercy God would grant us: freeing us from captivity, sending a son to die for us. It's all symbols back to us. The rainbow goes back to us, the sun goes back to us, the moon goes back to us. Everything on this earth refers back to God's people and God's mercy towards that people. No one else.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

points: The barren woman who did not bear is told to break forth into singing, for the children of the desolate are more than the children of the married wife. This is the promise of increase to a people who had been left desolate.

note.label: Isaiah 54: The Restoration of Zion

points: She is told to enlarge the place of her tent, stretch forth the curtains, and strengthen her stakes, because she will break forth on the right hand and on the left, and her seed will inherit the Gentiles and make the desolate cities inhabited.

note.label: Isaiah 54: The Restoration of Zion

points: She is told to fear not and not be ashamed, for she will forget the shame of her youth and the reproach of her widowhood.

note.label: Isaiah 54: The Restoration of Zion

points: The names given here are titles of the Most High: the Lord of hosts, thy redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, the God of the whole earth. When the Scripture reads a different name it is still the same God under a different title.

note.label: Isaiah 54: The Restoration of Zion

points: The Most High called her as a woman forsaken and grieved in spirit, a wife of youth who was refused. For a small moment He forsook her, but with great mercies He will gather her.

note.label: Isaiah 54: The Restoration of Zion

points: In a little wrath He hid His face for a moment, but with everlasting kindness He will have mercy on her. He compares this to the waters of Noah: as He swore the waters would no more cover the earth, so He has sworn He would not be wroth with her.

note.label: Isaiah 54: The Restoration of Zion

points: The mountains may depart and the hills be removed, but His kindness will not depart, and the covenant of His peace will not be removed.

note.label: Isaiah 54: The Restoration of Zion

points: To the afflicted one, tossed with tempest and not comforted, He promises to lay her stones with fair colours and her foundations with sapphires, her windows of agates, her gates of carbuncles, and all her borders of pleasant stones.

note.label: Isaiah 54: The Restoration of Zion

points: All her children will be taught of the Most High, and great will be the peace of her children.

note.label: Isaiah 54: The Restoration of Zion

points: In righteousness she will be established; she will be far from oppression and will not fear, and terror will not come near her.

note.label: Isaiah 54: The Restoration of Zion

points: Any who gather together against her do not do so by Him, and whoever gathers against her will fall for her sake.

note.label: Isaiah 54: The Restoration of Zion

points: He created the smith that blows the coals and brings forth an instrument for his work, and He created the waster to destroy. Both maker and destroyer are His.

note.label: Isaiah 54: The Restoration of Zion

points: No weapon formed against her will prosper, and every tongue that rises against her in judgment she will condemn. This is the heritage of the servants of the Most High, and their righteousness is of Him.
